questions.question_english: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 was enacted to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD). In which year did India sign the UNCRPD?
questions.explanation_english: India signed the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) on October 1, 2007, and ratified it in October 2007. Pursuant to its international commitments and in exercise of legislative powers under Article 253 of the Constitution of India (legislation for giving effect to international agreements), the Parliament of India enacted the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016. This statute replaced the earlier Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 to harmonize domestic legal provisions with the global human rights paradigm.
questions.explanation_hindi: भारत ने 1 अक्टूबर 2007 को दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के अधिकारों पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र सम्मेलन (UNCRPD) पर हस्ताक्षर किए तथा अक्टूबर 2007 में ही इसकी विधिवत पुष्टि (अनुसमर्थन) की। अंतरराष्ट्रीय दायित्वों को पूरा करने और भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 253 (अंतरराष्ट्रीय करारों को प्रभावी करने हेतु विधान) के तहत प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए भारतीय संसद ने दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 पारित किया। इस अधिनियम ने 1995 के पुराने दिव्यांगजन कानून का स्थान लिया ताकि भारतीय कानूनों को वैश्विक मानवाधिकार मानकों के अनुरूप बनाया जा सके।

questions.question_english: Which of the following paradigms reflects the core conceptual shift introduced by the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 compared to the earlier 1995 Act?
options_english: From a medical and charity-based model to a rights-based and social model
From integrated education to institutionalized special education
From a state-funded welfare model to a privately funded rehabilitation model
From mandatory quota-based employment to voluntary affirmative action
questions.explanation_english: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 marks an essential paradigm shift from the medical and charity-oriented approach of the 1995 legislation to a human rights-based and social model. The medical model viewed disability as an individual physical or mental deficit needing medical treatment, charity, or pity. In contrast, the rights-based social model, aligned with UNCRPD and Articles 14, 15, and 21 of the Indian Constitution, recognizes that disability is the outcome of the interaction between individuals with impairments and systemic environmental, institutional, and attitudinal barriers that hinder their full, equal, and dignified participation in society.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 वर्ष 1995 के कानून के चिकित्सा एवं दान-आधारित दृष्टिकोण से हटकर मानवाधिकार-आधारित और सामाजिक मॉडल की ओर एक महत्वपूर्ण वैचारिक बदलाव प्रस्तुत करता है। चिकित्सा मॉडल दिव्यांगता को व्यक्ति की शारीरिक या मानसिक कमी मानकर उपचार व दया का विषय समझता था। इसके विपरीत, संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14, 15 और 21 तथा UNCRPD के सिद्धांतों पर आधारित सामाजिक मॉडल यह मानता है कि दिव्यांगता किसी व्यक्ति की शारीरिक स्थिति और समाज में मौजूद भौतिक, संस्थागत व दृष्टिकोण संबंधी बाधाओं के बीच की अंतःक्रिया का परिणाम है, जो उसके पूर्ण व गरिमापूर्ण समावेशन को रोकती है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) From a medical and charity-based model to a rights-based and social model

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: a rights-based and social model The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 marks a major paradigm shift from the medical and charity-oriented approach of the 1995 legislation to a human rights-based and social model. This paradigm emphasizes dignity, individual autonomy, non-discrimination, full inclusion, and equal opportunity, viewing disability as an interaction between impairments and environmental barriers.

questions.question_english: Under the RPwD Act, 2016, the term "appropriate Government" for schools established, owned, or controlled by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD refers to which of the following?
options_english: The Union Ministry of Education, Government of India
The Rehabilitation Council of India, Statutory Body
The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, Local Authority
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(b) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'appropriate Government' is defined in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by the Central Government as the Central Government, and in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by a State Government or Union Territory administration as that respective Government or administration. For schools established, managed, or funded by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, the appropriate Government is the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD). The appropriate Government carries statutory responsibilities under the Act for providing barrier-free infrastructure, inclusive education, teacher training, and reasonable accommodations.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 2(b) के अनुसार 'समुचित सरकार' का अर्थ केंद्र सरकार के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए केंद्र सरकार तथा राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए संबंधित राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन है। शिक्षा निदेशालय, GNCTD द्वारा संचालित अथवा वित्तपोषित विद्यालयों के लिए 'समुचित सरकार' राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार (GNCTD) है। समुचित सरकार होने के नाते दिल्ली सरकार पर इन विद्यालयों में बाधा-मुक्त वातावरण, समावेशी शिक्षा, विशेष शिक्षक प्रशिक्षण तथा उचित समायोजन सुनिश्चित करने का वैधानिक दायित्व है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The Government of NCT of Delhi

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016, the appropriate government for an educational institution owned, controlled, or substantially financed by a State Government or Union Territory administration is that respective government. Therefore, for schools established or run by the Directorate of Education in Delhi, the Government of NCT of Delhi acts as the appropriate government.

questions.question_english: Section 3 of the RPwD Act, 2016 guarantees equality and non-discrimination. Which of the following principles forms the foundation of non-discrimination under this section?
options_english: Universal financial assistance
Exemptions from standard educational curricula
Mandatory separate schooling
Reasonable accommodation
questions.explanation_english: Section 3 of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates equality and non-discrimination for persons with disabilities. Subsection (5) of Section 3 specifically provides that the appropriate Government shall take necessary steps to ensure reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. 'Reasonable accommodation' is defined under Section 2(y) as necessary and appropriate modification and adjustments, not imposing a disproportionate or undue burden in a particular case, to ensure to persons with disabilities the enjoyment or exercise of rights equally with others. This concept serves as the foundational legal tool to achieve substantive equality (as opposed to mere formal equality) under Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 3 दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के लिए समानता और गैर-भेदभाव की गारंटी देती है। धारा 3(5) स्पष्ट रूप से यह प्रावधान करती है कि समुचित सरकार दिव्यांगजनों के लिए उचित समायोजन सुनिश्चित करने हेतु आवश्यक कदम उठाएगी। धारा 2(y) के अनुसार, 'उचित समायोजन' का अर्थ बिना किसी अनुचित या अत्यधिक बोझ के किए गए वे आवश्यक व उपयुक्त रूपांतरण एवं अनुकूलन हैं, जो दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों को अन्य लोगों के समान अपने अधिकारों और मौलिक स्वतंत्रताओं का उपभोग करने में सक्षम बनाते हैं। यह सिद्धांत संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 और 15 के तहत वास्तविक समानता प्राप्त करने का आधार है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Reasonable accommodation

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 3 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 mandates equality and non- discrimination for individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodation is the core principle underlying non-discrimination, requiring necessary and appropriate modifications or adjustments to ensure persons with disabilities enjoy and exercise all constitutional rights and fundamental freedoms on an equal basis with others.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The RPwD Act, 2016 mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality and a life with dignity.
Reason (R): The Act prohibits the deprivation of personal liberty of any person solely on the ground of disability.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both statements are correct statutory provisions under the RPwD Act, 2016, but Reason (R) is not the causal explanation of Assertion (A). Section 3(1) of the Act mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality, life with dignity, and respect for their integrity equally with others, directly giving effect to Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution. Meanwhile, Section 4(1) provides that no person shall be deprived of his or her personal liberty only on the ground of disability. Although both are statutory rights safeguarding dignity and freedom, the prohibition against deprivation of personal liberty is an independent legal guarantee under Section 4 and does not logically or causally explain why the State must ensure equality and dignity under Section 3.
questions.explanation_hindi: दोनों कथन RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 के तहत सत्य वैधानिक प्रावधान हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। धारा 3(1) यह अनिवार्य करती है कि समुचित सरकार यह सुनिश्चित करे कि दिव्यांग व्यक्ति समानता के अधिकार, गरिमापूर्ण जीवन तथा अपनी अखंडता के सम्मान का उपभोग दूसरों के समान करें (संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 और 21 के अनुरूप)। वहीं, धारा 4(1) यह प्रावधान करती है कि किसी भी व्यक्ति को केवल दिव्यांगता के आधार पर उसकी व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा। दोनों प्रावधान महत्वपूर्ण मानवीय और मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा करते हैं, किंतु व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता के हनन का निषेध, समानता व गरिमा सुनिश्चित करने के स्वतंत्र राज्यीय दायित्व का व्याख्यात्मक कारण नहीं है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of A Section 3 mandates that the appropriate government ensures equality, life with dignity, and respect for integrity for persons with disabilities. The statute also prohibits the unlawful deprivation of personal liberty based solely on disability. While both statutory principles are true and established under the Act, prohibition of liberty deprivation serves as an independent guarantee rather than direct explanation.

questions.question_english: The RPwD Act, 2016 specifies certain conditions under which a person with disability might be subjected to differential treatment. Which of the following represents a legally valid ground for such action under the Act?
options_english: When it significantly reduces the operational and administrative burden on management
When shown as a proportionate means to achieve a legitimate aim
When the parent or legal guardian of the child explicitly consents to it
When the institution demonstrates a complete lack of adequate financial resources
questions.explanation_english: Section 3(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 strictly prohibits discrimination against any person with disability on the ground of disability, unless it is shown that the impugned act or omission is a 'proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim'. The law imposes a rigorous proportionality test, meaning differential treatment cannot be excused on grounds of administrative convenience, financial incapacity, institutional preferences, or parental consent. Any departure from non-discrimination must serve a legitimate statutory purpose and must be strictly proportionate, ensuring that arbitrary distinctions violate Article 14 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 3(1) दिव्यांगता के आधार पर किसी भी प्रकार के भेदभाव को पूरी तरह प्रतिबंधित करती है, जब तक कि यह सिद्ध न कर दिया जाए कि ऐसा कृत्य या चूक 'किसी वैध उद्देश्य को प्राप्त करने का एक आनुपातिक साधन' (proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim) है। यह कानून कड़े आनुपातिकता परीक्षण को लागू करता है; अतः प्रशासनिक सुविधा, वित्तीय तंगी या अभिभावकों की सहमति को विभेदकारी व्यवहार का कानूनी आधार नहीं बनाया जा सकता। किसी भी भिन्न व्यवहार को वैध कानूनी उद्देश्य की कसौटी पर खरा उतरना होगा ताकि संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 का उल्लंघन न हो।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) When shown as a proportionate means to achieve a legitimate aim

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: achieve a legitimate aim The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 permits differential treatment of a person with a disability only under specific legal exceptions. Such treatment is valid solely when it can be objectively demonstrated that the action or distinction constitutes a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim, thereby protecting individuals against arbitrary administrative discrimination or convenience-based exclusions.

questions.question_english: According to the RPwD Act, 2016, who is fundamentally responsible for providing "reasonable accommodation" to a student with a disability?
options_english: The State Medical Board
The parents or guardians of the student
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
The respective educational institution
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, the legal responsibility of providing reasonable accommodation to students with disabilities is placed squarely on the respective educational institutions funded or recognized by the government and local authorities. Section 16(iii) explicitly obligates educational institutions to provide reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements. This includes physical accessibility (ramps, lifts, accessible toilets), adapted pedagogical tools, appropriate learning materials (Braille, large print, audio formats), assistive technologies, and examination accommodations. The burden cannot be transferred to the parents or external agencies.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16 के अंतर्गत दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों को उचित समायोजन प्रदान करने का वैधानिक दायित्व प्रत्यक्ष रूप से संबंधित शिक्षण संस्थान (The respective educational institution) पर डाला गया है। धारा 16(iii) के अनुसार, सरकार और स्थानीय निकायों द्वारा वित्तपोषित या मान्यता प्राप्त सभी शिक्षण संस्थानों का यह कर्तव्य है कि वे प्रत्येक दिव्यांग विद्यार्थी की व्यक्तिगत जरूरतों के अनुरूप उचित समायोजन उपलब्ध कराएं। इसमें भौतिक सुगमता (रैंप, सुलभ शौचालय), अनुकूलित शिक्षण सहायक सामग्री (ब्रेल, ऑडियो), सहायक उपकरण तथा परीक्षा संबंधी रियायतें शामिल हैं। यह दायित्व अभिभावकों पर नहीं छोड़ा जा सकता।

questions.question_english: What is the fundamental difference between a "person with disability" and a "person with benchmark disability" as defined in the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: Benchmark disability requires at least 40% certified specified disability, while disability covers any long-term impairment
Benchmark disability applies strictly to physical impairments, whereas disability covers all physical and mental impairments
Benchmark disability applies exclusively to adult citizens, whereas general disability applies to both children and adults
Benchmark disability requires a mandatory income certificate, whereas general disability classification requires no financial proof
questions.explanation_english:
The RPwD Act, 2016 maintains a vital distinction between general disability and benchmark disability:
1. Section 2(s) defines a 'person with disability' as a person with long-term physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders their full and effective participation in society equally with others.
2. Section 2(r) defines a 'person with benchmark disability' as a person with not less than forty percent (40%) of a specified disability (as certified by a certifying medical authority), or a person with disability where specified disability has not been defined in measurable terms.
A certified benchmark disability (minimum 40%) is a statutory prerequisite to claim reservations in higher educational institutions (Section 32, minimum 5%), government employment (Section 34, minimum 4%), free education up to 18 years of age (Section 31), and priority in government welfare schemes.
questions.explanation_hindi:
RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 में सामान्य दिव्यांगता और बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता के बीच एक स्पष्ट विधिक अंतर है:
1. धारा 2(s) के तहत 'दिव्यांग व्यक्ति' वह है जिसे कोई भी दीर्घकालिक शारीरिक, मानसिक, बौद्धिक या संवेदी दुर्बलता हो, जो विभिन्न बाधाओं के साथ परस्पर क्रिया में समाज में उसके पूर्ण और समान समावेशन में रुकावट डालती है।
2. धारा 2(r) के तहत 'बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाला व्यक्ति' वह है जिसके पास सक्षम चिकित्सा प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी कम से कम 40% (चालीस प्रतिशत) विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगता का प्रमाणपत्र हो।
यह न्यूनतम 40% की अर्हता उच्च शिक्षण संस्थानों में आरक्षण (धारा 32 के तहत न्यूनतम 5%), सरकारी नौकरियों में आरक्षण (धारा 34 के तहत न्यूनतम 4%) तथा 6 से 18 वर्ष तक निःशुल्क शिक्षा (धारा 31) जैसी सकारात्मक कार्रवाइयों का लाभ उठाने के लिए अनिवार्य है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Benchmark disability requires at least 40% specified disability, while disability covers any long-term impairment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: specified disability, while disability covers any long-term impairment The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 defines a person with disability as anyone with a long-term physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairment. In contrast, a person with benchmark disability specifically refers to an individual certified with not less than forty percent of a specified disability, which serves as the threshold for claiming statutory reservations and benefits.

questions.question_english: How many specified disabilities are recognized under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?
questions.explanation_english: The Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 recognizes 21 specified disabilities, substantially expanding the coverage from the 7 conditions recognized under the repealed Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995. The 21 categories include physical disabilities (locomotor disability, leprosy cured, cerebral palsy, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy, acid attack victims, blindness, low-vision, deaf, hard of hearing, speech and language disability), intellectual disabilities (specific learning disabilities, autism spectrum disorder), mental illness, chronic neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease), blood disorders (haemophilia, thalassemia, sickle cell disease), and multiple disabilities. Under Section 56, the Central Government also possesses the statutory power to notify additional conditions.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के तहत कुल 21 विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं को मान्यता प्रदान की गई है, जो कि 1995 के पुराने कानून में मान्यता प्राप्त 7 दिव्यांगताओं से तीन गुना अधिक है। इन 21 श्रेणियों में शारीरिक अक्षमताएँ (चलन दिव्यांगता, कुष्ठ रोग मुक्त, सेरेब्रल पाल्सी, बौनापन, मस्कुलर डिस्ट्रॉफी, एसिड अटैक पीड़ित, दृष्टिहीनता, अल्प दृष्टि, बधिर, श्रवण बाधित, वाक् एवं भाषा दिव्यांगता), बौद्धिक अक्षमता (विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता, ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम), मानसिक रुग्णता, दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी विकार (मल्टीपल स्केलेरोसिस, पार्किंसंस रोग), रक्त विकार (हीमोफिलिया, थैलेसीमिया, सिकल सेल रोग) और बहु-दिव्यांगता शामिल हैं। धारा 56 के तहत केंद्र सरकार नई दिव्यांगताओं को जोड़ने हेतु अधिकृत है।

questions.question_english: Which of the following is categorized as a "blood disorder" under the Schedule of the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: Parkinson's disease
Multiple Sclerosis
Muscular Dystrophy
Thalassemia
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4 of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Blood Disorders' form a distinct category of specified disabilities comprising three severe conditions: (i) Thalassemia, (ii) Haemophilia, and (iii) Sickle Cell Disease. Thalassemia is a group of inherited blood disorders characterized by reduced or absent production of normal haemoglobin, necessitating lifelong blood transfusions. Regarding the other options: Parkinson's disease and Multiple Sclerosis are classified under 'Chronic Neurological Conditions' (Section 1(D) of the Schedule), while Muscular Dystrophy is categorized under 'Locomotor Disability' (Section 1(A)(d) of the Schedule).
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 4 के अंतर्गत 'रक्त विकार' (Blood Disorders) के रूप में तीन वंशानुगत रक्त रोगों को विनिर्दिष्ट किया गया है: (i) थैलेसीमिया, (ii) हीमोफिलिया, और (iii) सिकल सेल रोग। थैलेसीमिया असामान्य हीमोग्लोबिन उत्पादन का एक गंभीर विकार है जिसके कारण रोगी को नियमित रूप से रक्त चढ़ाने (blood transfusion) की आवश्यकता होती है। अन्य विकल्पों में: पार्किंसंस रोग और मल्टीपल स्केलेरोसिस 'दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी स्थितियों' के तहत आते हैं, जबकि मस्कुलर डिस्ट्रॉफी 'चलन दिव्यांगता' का भाग है।

Thalassemia, along with hemophilia and sickle cell disease, is explicitly listed under blood disorders, recognizing the long-term impact of periodic transfusions, medical management, and physiological complications associated with severe hereditary blood conditions.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2 of the Schedule to the RPwD Act, 2016, 'Specific Learning Disabilities' (SLD) is defined as a heterogeneous group of conditions wherein there is a deficit in processing language, spoken or written, that may manifest itself as a difficulty to comprehend, speak, read, write, spell, or to do mathematical calculations. It specifically includes conditions such as Dyslexia (reading difficulty), Dysgraphia (writing and fine motor expression difficulty), and Dyscalculia (arithmetical calculation difficulty). In school education, identifying SLD is essential for school administrators to implement CBSE examination concessions, provide scribes, offer compensatory time, and design individualized education plans (IEPs).
questions.explanation_hindi: RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 2 के तहत 'विशिष्ट अधिगम दिव्यांगता' (Specific Learning Disabilities - SLD) को भाषा प्रसंस्करण (मौखिक या लिखित) में कमी से उत्पन्न स्थितियों के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है, जो समझने, बोलने, पढ़ने, लिखने, वर्तनी या गणितीय गणना करने में कठिनाई के रूप में प्रकट होती है। इसमें विशेष रूप से डिस्लेक्सिया (पढ़ने में कठिनाई), डिस्ग्राफिया (लिखने में कठिनाई) और डिस्केल्कुलिया (गणितीय गणना में कठिनाई) शामिल हैं। विद्यालय प्रबंधन और प्रधानाचार्यों के लिए इनकी पहचान करना आवश्यक है ताकि सीबीएसई एवं बोर्ड नियमों के तहत ऐसे विद्यार्थियों को स्क्राइब (लेखक), अतिरिक्त समय और उपचारात्मक शिक्षण उपलब्ध कराया जा सके।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Dyslexia, dysgraphia, and dyscalculia

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016, specific learning disabilities refer to a heterogeneous group of conditions affecting the processing of language, spoken or written. It specifically encompasses conditions such as dyslexia affecting reading, dysgraphia affecting written expression, and dyscalculia affecting mathematical calculations, requiring targeted pedagogical support and educational accommodations.

questions.question_english: Which authority is responsible for certifying a person as having a "benchmark disability" for the purpose of availing benefits under the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: The Principal of the recognized educational institution last attended by the candidate
A registered rehabilitation professional certified by the Rehabilitation Council of India
The Chief Medical Officer or a notified Government medical board
The State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities appointed by the Government
questions.explanation_english: Under Sections 56, 57, and 58 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 read with the RPwD Rules, 2017, the power to assess disability and issue a certificate of benchmark disability is vested exclusively in the notified 'certifying authority'. This certifying authority comprises the Chief Medical Officer (CMO), Chief District Medical Officer, or a notified Government Medical Board consisting of specialized medical officers in relevant fields (e.g., orthopaedician, ophthalmologist, ENT specialist, psychiatrist/clinical psychologist). Educational institution heads, RCI professionals, or Disability Commissioners lack statutory jurisdiction to issue disability certificates, although school authorities must verify such valid medical certificates (or UDID cards) when granting statutory reservations and accommodations.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 56, 57 और 58 तथा संबंधित नियमावली के तहत बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता का मूल्यांकन करने और प्रमाणपत्र जारी करने का अनन्य विधिक अधिकार केवल अधिसूचित 'प्रमाणन प्राधिकारी' (Certifying Authority) को प्राप्त है। यह प्राधिकारी मुख्य चिकित्सा अधिकारी (CMO), जिला चिकित्सा अधिकारी या सरकारी विशेषज्ञों से युक्त अधिसूचित मेडिकल बोर्ड होता है। विद्यालय के प्रधानाचार्य, RCI पेशेवर या राज्य दिव्यांगजन आयुक्त को दिव्यांगता प्रमाणपत्र जारी करने का अधिकार नहीं है। तथापि, विद्यालयों में 5% आरक्षण और परीक्षा संबंधी रियायतें देने के लिए प्रधानाचार्यों द्वारा इस वैध मेडिकल बोर्ड प्रमाणपत्र (या UDID कार्ड) का सत्यापन किया जाता है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The Chief Medical Officer or a notified Government medical board

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Government medical board The process of certifying benchmark disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 requires an official evaluation by a designated medical authority. The Chief Medical Officer or a notified Government medical board possesses the sole statutory competence to issue official disability certificates, evaluating the nature and extent of impairment required to access government schemes and affirmative action reservations.

questions.question_hindi: RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी स्थिति 'दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी स्थिति' (Chronic Neurological Conditions) के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत है?
options_hindi: हीमोफिलिया
कुष्ठ रोग मुक्त व्यक्ति

questions.question_english: Which of the following conditions is classified under "Chronic Neurological Conditions" in the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: Hemophilia
Leprosy cured person
Autism spectrum disorder
Parkinson's disease
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(D) of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Chronic Neurological Conditions' includes two specified medical conditions: (i) Multiple Sclerosis, and (ii) Parkinson's disease. Parkinson's disease is defined as a progressive disease of the nervous system marked by tremor, muscular rigidity, and slow, imprecise movement, chiefly affecting middle-aged and elderly people, associated with degeneration of the basal ganglia of the brain and a deficiency of the neurotransmitter dopamine. Among the other choices, Hemophilia is a Blood Disorder (Section 4), Leprosy Cured Person is classified under Locomotor Disability (Section 1(A)(b)), and Autism Spectrum Disorder is classified under Intellectual Disability / Neurodevelopmental conditions (Section 2).
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 1(D) के अनुसार 'दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी स्थिति' (Chronic Neurological Conditions) के अंतर्गत दो प्रमुख रोगों को विनिर्दिष्ट किया गया है: (i) मल्टीपल स्केलेरोसिस, और (ii) पार्किंसंस रोग। पार्किंसंस रोग केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र का एक प्रगतिशील विकार है जो शरीर के कंपन, कठोरता और शारीरिक संतुलन व गति में असमर्थता पैदा करता है। अन्य विकल्पों में, हीमोफिलिया 'रक्त विकार' है, कुष्ठ रोग मुक्त व्यक्ति 'चलन दिव्यांगता' का अंग है, और ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम विकार 'बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता' के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Parkinson's disease

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 includes chronic neurological conditions within its list of specified disabilities. Parkinson's disease, characterized by progressive nervous system disorder affecting movement, tremor, stiffness, and balance, is classified under chronic neurological conditions, alongside multiple sclerosis, providing statutory recognition and entitlements to affected individuals requiring continuous healthcare and social support.

questions.question_hindi: दिल्ली सरकार के एक विद्यालय में कक्षा 8 का एक विद्यार्थी बोलने और लिखने के लिए आवश्यक मांसपेशियों की गति में समन्वय करने में अत्यधिक कठिनाई प्रदर्शित करता है। मेडिकल प्रमाणपत्र जन्म से पूर्व (before birth) मस्तिष्क में हुई चोट का संकेत देता है। RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 के तहत यह किस विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगता श्रेणी के अंतर्गत आता है?

मस्कुलर डिस्ट्रॉफी (Muscular Dystrophy)

विशिष्ट अधिगम दिव्यांगता (Specific Learning Disability)

questions.question_english: A Class VIII student in a Delhi Government school exhibits extreme difficulty in coordinating muscle movements required for speaking and writing. The medical certificate indicates an injury to the brain that occurred before birth. Under which specified disability category of the RPwD Act, 2016 does this fall?
options_english: Cerebral Palsy
Muscular Dystrophy
Multiple Sclerosis
Specific Learning Disability
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(A)(c) of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Cerebral Palsy' is classified under Locomotor Disability and is defined as a non-progressive condition characterized by abnormal motor control posture resulting from brain insult or injuries occurring in the pre-natal, peri-natal, or infant period of development. The clinical indicators presented in the question—extreme difficulty in muscle coordination affecting speech and writing arising from brain injury occurring before birth (pre-natal)—precisely match the legal definition of Cerebral Palsy. In inclusive schools, students with cerebral palsy are legally entitled under Section 16 to assistive speech tech, adapted furniture, mobility devices, scribes, and compensatory exam time.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 1(A)(c) के अनुसार, 'प्रमस्तिष्कीय घात' (Cerebral Palsy) को चलन दिव्यांगता के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत किया गया है। इसे जन्म से पूर्व (pre-natal), जन्म के दौरान या शैशवावस्था में मस्तिष्क को हुई क्षति के कारण उत्पन्न मोटर नियंत्रण और मुद्रा की गैर-प्रगतिशील स्थिति के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। प्रश्न में प्रस्तुत लक्षण (जन्म से पूर्व मस्तिष्क क्षति के कारण बोलने और लिखने में मांसपेशियों के समन्वय में गंभीर समस्या) पूर्णतः सेरेब्रल पाल्सी की वैधानिक परिभाषा से मेल खाते हैं। समावेशी शिक्षा के तहत धारा 16 के अनुसार विद्यालय ऐसे विद्यार्थियों को सहायक उपकरण, सुलभ बैठने की व्यवस्था और परीक्षा में प्रतिपूरक समय व लेखक उपलब्ध कराने के लिए बाध्य हैं।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Cerebral Palsy

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Cerebral palsy is defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 as a non-progressive neurological condition caused by brain damage occurring before, during, or shortly after birth. It primarily affects muscle coordination, movement, posture, speech, and motor skills, necessitating tailored physical therapy, assistive technology, and adapted learning strategies within inclusive educational institutions.

questions.question_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की अनुसूची के अंतर्गत 'बधिर-अंधता' (Deafblindness) को निम्नलिखित में से किस व्यापक श्रेणी के तहत वर्गीकृत किया गया है?
options_hindi: शारीरिक दिव्यांगता (Physical Disability)
बहु-दिव्यांगता (Multiple Disabilities)
बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता (Intellectual Disability)
दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी स्थितियां (Chronic Neurological Conditions)

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: Under the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, under which of the following broad classifications is 'Deafblindness' categorized?
options_english: Physical Disability
Multiple Disabilities
Intellectual Disability
Chronic Neurological Conditions
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 (specifying disabilities under Section 2(zc)), disabilities are broadly organized into specified categories including Physical Disability, Intellectual Disability, Mental Illness, Disabilities caused by Chronic Neurological Conditions & Blood Disorders, and Multiple Disabilities.

Section 2(zc) read with the Schedule defines 'Multiple Disabilities' as the occurrence of more than one of the specified disabilities in an individual, explicitly including 'Deafblindness'. Deafblindness is characterized as a distinct condition caused by a combination of both severe visual and hearing impairments, creating severe communication, developmental, educational, and mobility challenges. It cannot be accommodated simply as a single sensory impairment, which is why Parliament designated it under the Multiple Disabilities category to ensure specialized rehabilitation, tactile communication methods, and assistive pedagogical aids in educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(zc) के साथ पठित अनुसूची (Schedule) में विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं (Specified Disabilities) को विभिन्न श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया गया है। इनमें शारीरिक दिव्यांगता, बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता, मानसिक रुग्णता, दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी एवं रक्त विकार तथा 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' शामिल हैं।

अनुसूची के पैरा 5 के अंतर्गत 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' (Multiple Disabilities) के तहत दो या दो से अधिक विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं के संयोजन को शामिल किया गया है, जिसमें स्पष्ट रूप से 'बधिर-अंधता' (Deafblindness) का उल्लेख किया गया है। बधिर-अंधता दृष्टि और श्रवण दोनों प्रकार की गंभीर क्षतियों का ऐसा मिला-जुला रूप है जिसके कारण गंभीर संचार, विकासात्मक और अधिगम संबंधी बाधाएं उत्पन्न होती हैं। इसलिए कानून में इसे एकल संवेदी बाधा न मानकर 'बहु-दिव्यांगता' के अंतर्गत रखा गया है ताकि ऐसे शिक्षार्थियों को विशेष स्पर्श संचार (स्पर्श ब्रेल), अनुरूपित शिक्षण और पुनर्वास सेवाएं प्रदान की जा सकें।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Multiple Disabilities

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Deafblindness is a condition combining severe visual and hearing impairments, resulting in unique communication and developmental challenges. Under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016, deafblindness is categorized under the broader classification of multiple disabilities, which covers combination of two or more specified disabilities occurring simultaneously in an individual.

questions.question_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 के प्रावधानों के अंतर्गत वैधानिक पद 'उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता वाला व्यक्ति' (Person with high support needs) से क्या अभिप्राय है?
options_hindi: ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसे निरंतर चिकित्सा उपचार हेतु राज्य से आजीवन और सघन वित्तीय सहायता की आवश्यकता होती है
बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता से युक्त ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसे दैनिक जीवन और स्वतंत्र क्रियाशीलता हेतु सघन शारीरिक, मनोवैज्ञानिक या अन्य सहायता की आवश्यकता होती है
ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसका राज्य द्वारा वित्तपोषित विशेष आवासीय विद्यालय में संस्थागत प्रवेश कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य हो
ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसकी प्रमाणित बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता का प्रतिशत कड़ाई से 80% की सीमा से अधिक मूल्यांकित किया गया हो

questions.question_english: Under the provisions of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, what is meant by the statutory term 'person with high support needs'?
options_english: An individual who requires continuous and intensive financial assistance from the state for ongoing medical treatment
A person with benchmark disability who needs intensive physical, psychological, or other support for daily living and independent functioning
A person who requires mandatory institutionalization and admission to a government-funded special residential school
A person whose certified benchmark disability percentage is evaluated to be strictly in excess of an 80% threshold
questions.explanation_english:
According to Section 2(t) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, a 'person with high support' means a person with benchmark disability certified under Section 58(2) of the Act who needs high support.

Section 2(l) defines 'high support' as an intensive support—physical, psychological, and otherwise—which may be required by a person with benchmark disability for daily activities, to take independent and informed decisions, to access facilities, and to participate in all areas of life including education, employment, and family and community life. Under Section 38, any person with benchmark disability (or their caregiver/organization) who requires high support can apply to the designated assessment authority to seek prioritized support services, attendant care, and specialized state assistance.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(t) के अनुसार, 'उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता वाले व्यक्ति' (Person with high support) से धारा 58(2) के तहत प्रमाणित बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता से युक्त ऐसा व्यक्ति अभिप्रेत है जिसे उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता होती है।

questions.question_english: Pursuant to Section 31 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, up to what age is every child with a benchmark disability guaranteed the statutory right to free education?
options_english: 14 years
16 years
18 years

questions.explanation_english:
Section 31(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 contains a non-obstante clause that explicitly expands upon the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. It stipulates:
'Notwithstanding anything contained in the Rights of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, every child with benchmark disability between the age of six to eighteen years shall have the right to free education in a neighbourhood school, or in a special school, of his choice.'

While the RTE Act guarantees free education to general children up to the age of 14 years (elementary education from classes 1 to 8), Section 31 of the RPwD Act deliberately extends this entitlement up to the age of 18 years (covering secondary and senior secondary schooling). This statutory recognition accommodates potential late enrollment, medical interruptions, and the extended learning pace of children with disabilities.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 31(1) में एक विशिष्ट प्रावधान है जो निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 के प्रावधानों का विस्तार करता है। धारा 31(1) के अनुसार:
'निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 में किसी बात के होते हुए भी, छह से अठारह वर्ष की आयु के बीच बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले प्रत्येक बच्चे को अपनी पसंद के पड़ोस के विद्यालय या किसी विशेष विद्यालय में निःशुल्क शिक्षा प्राप्त करने का अधिकार होगा।'

सामान्य बच्चों के लिए आरटीई अधिनियम, 2009 के तहत निःशुल्क शिक्षा 6 से 14 वर्ष (कक्षा 8 तक) के लिए सुनिश्चित है, जबकि RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 31 इस विधिक अधिकार को 18 वर्ष (कक्षा 12/उच्च माध्यमिक स्तर) तक बढ़ाती है ताकि दिव्यांग बच्चों को उनकी विशिष्ट आवश्यकताओं और उपचार संबंधी विलंब के बावजूद माध्यमिक स्तर तक पूर्णतः निःशुल्क शिक्षा मिल सके।

questions.question_english: Under Section 32 of the RPwD Act, 2016, all government institutions of higher education and other higher educational institutions receiving aid from the Government are required to reserve what minimum percentage of seats for persons with benchmark disabilities?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 32(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 explicitly provides:
'All Government institutions of higher education and other higher education institutions receiving aid from the Government shall reserve not less than five per cent seats for persons with benchmark disabilities.'

Candidates often confuse this with employment reservation: under Section 34 of the Act, reservation in public sector employment is set at a minimum of 4%, whereas under Section 32, reservation in government and government-aided institutions of higher education is set at not less than 5%. Furthermore, Section 32(2) provides an upper age relaxation of 5 years for admission to such higher educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 32(1) स्पष्ट रूप से यह अधिदेशित करती है:
'उच्च शिक्षा के सभी सरकारी संस्थान और सरकार से सहायता प्राप्त अन्य उच्च शिक्षा संस्थान बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए कम से कम पांच प्रतिशत (5%) सीटें आरक्षित करेंगे।'

ध्यान रहे कि सार्वजनिक रोजगार में धारा 34 के तहत बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों के लिए न्यूनतम 4% आरक्षण का प्रावधान है, जबकि उच्च शिक्षण संस्थानों (महाविद्यालयों/विश्वविद्यालयों) में प्रवेश हेतु धारा 32 के तहत यह कोटा 'न्यूनतम 5%' निर्धारित किया गया है। इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 32(2) के तहत उच्च शिक्षा में प्रवेश के लिए अधिकतम आयु सीमा में 5 वर्ष की छूट का भी वैधानिक प्रावधान है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 5%

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 32 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 mandates that all government institutions of higher education and institutions receiving government aid must reserve a minimum of five percent of available seats for persons with benchmark disabilities. This provision aims to promote higher educational attainment and career development opportunities for disabled students nationwide.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): A school Principal cannot deny admission to a child with a benchmark disability solely on the ground of their disability.
Reason (R): Section 16 of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates that all educational institutions funded or recognized by the appropriate government must provide inclusive education and admit children with disabilities without discrimination.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the direct statutory justification and correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 provides that the appropriate government and local authorities shall ensure that all educational institutions funded or recognized by them provide inclusive education to children with disabilities. Sub-clause (i) of Section 16 specifically mandates that institutions must 'admit them without discrimination and provide education and opportunities for sports and recreation activities equally with others'.

Therefore, any refusal by a school principal or administrative authority to admit a student on the ground of disability is a direct violation of Section 16, attracting penal consequences under Section 89 and Section 91/92 of the Act. Hence, R correctly explains A.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों पूर्णतः सत्य हैं, तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही विधिक स्पष्टीकरण प्रस्तुत करता है।

दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 16 समुचित सरकारों और स्थानीय प्राधिकारियों पर यह वैधानिक दायित्व डालती है कि वे अपने द्वारा वित्तपोषित अथवा मान्यता प्राप्त सभी शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में दिव्यांग बच्चों को समावेशी शिक्षा प्रदान करें। धारा 16(i) स्पष्ट आदेश देती है कि शिक्षण संस्थान 'उन्हें बिना किसी भेदभाव के प्रवेश देंगे और दूसरों के समान ही खेल व मनोरंजन गतिविधियों के अवसर तथा शिक्षा प्रदान करेंगे'।

अतः किसी विद्यालय के प्राचार्य द्वारा दिव्यांगता के आधार पर किसी बच्चे को प्रवेश देने से मना करना गैर-कानूनी और दंडनीय है। इस प्रकार, (R) सीधे तौर पर (A) का सही कारण और विधिक आधार स्पष्ट करता है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation_english:
Section 32(2) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 states:
'The persons with benchmark disabilities shall be given an upper age relaxation of five years for admission in institutions of higher education.'

This statutory dispensation is intended to offset the substantial impediments that students with benchmark disabilities often confront during their schooling years—such as surgical interventions, extensive medical therapies, protracted rehabilitation, or lack of accessible infrastructure—which frequently delay their completion of qualifying examinations.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 32(2) में स्पष्ट रूप से यह प्रावधान किया गया है:
'उच्च शिक्षा के संस्थानों में प्रवेश के लिए बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले व्यक्तियों को अधिकतम आयु सीमा में पांच वर्ष (5 years) की छूट दी जाएगी।'

यह विधिक छूट इसलिए प्रदान की गई है क्योंकि बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता से ग्रस्त विद्यार्थियों को अपनी प्रारंभिक एवं माध्यमिक स्कूली शिक्षा के दौरान चिकित्सा उपचार, शल्यक्रियाओं, थेरेपी अथवा सुगम्यता की कमी के कारण अक्सर शैक्षणिक रुकावटों या विलंब का सामना करना पड़ता है। अतः 5 वर्ष की यह आयु-छूट उन्हें उच्च शिक्षा में समान अवसर प्रदान करती है।

questions.question_english: To facilitate fair examination participation for children with disabilities, Central and State examination boards provide designated accommodations. Which of the following is NOT a permissible or mandated accommodation?
options_english: Provision of an amanuensis (scribe) or reader
Complete exemption from all continuous and comprehensive evaluations (CCE) and assessments
Compensatory extra time to complete the examination
Alternative objective or adapted questions in lieu of descriptive or visual/diagram-based questions
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 16(vi) of the RPwD Act, 2016 and examination guidelines issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MSJE), CBSE, and State Boards, reasonable accommodations during examinations include:
1. Provision of an amanuensis (scribe), reader, or lab assistant.
2. Compensatory time of not less than 20 minutes per hour of examination.
3. Adapted/alternative questions in lieu of visual diagrams or map-work for visually impaired candidates.
4. Facility to use assistive technology, computers, Braille sheets, or large-print question papers.
5. Exemption from second/third language requirements.

However, 'complete exemption from all continuous and comprehensive evaluations (CCE)' is NOT a permissible accommodation. Evaluation and assessment are indispensable components of the educational process to identify learning gaps and design individualized education plans (IEPs). Rather than exempting a child entirely from assessment, the modes, tools, and formatting of evaluation must be suitably adapted.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16(vi) तथा केंद्रीय सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय और विभिन्न परीक्षा बोर्डों (जैसे CBSE) द्वारा जारी दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार परीक्षा में दी जाने वाली सुविधाओं में निम्नलिखित शामिल हैं:
1. श्रुतलेखक (स्क्राइब), वाचक अथवा प्रयोगशाला सहायक की सुविधा।
2. प्रति घंटे कम से कम 20 मिनट का प्रतिपूरक (अतिरिक्त) समय।
3. दृष्टिबाधित परीक्षार्थियों के लिए रेखाचित्रों/मानचित्रों के स्थान पर वैकल्पिक वस्तुनिष्ठ प्रश्न।
4. ब्रेल लिपि, बड़े अक्षरों वाले प्रश्नपत्र या कंप्यूटर का उपयोग करने की अनुमति।
5. द्वितीय/तृतीय भाषा के अध्ययन से छूट।

किंतु 'समस्त सतत एवं व्यापक मूल्यांकन (CCE) और आकलनों से पूर्ण छूट' कोई मान्य सुविधा नहीं है। मूल्यांकन विद्यार्थी के शैक्षणिक विकास व अधिगम स्तर को जानने का अनिवार्य अंग है। समावेशी शिक्षा का उद्देश्य मूल्यांकन को पूरी तरह समाप्त करना नहीं, बल्कि मूल्यांकन की पद्धतियों को बच्चे की दिव्यांगता के अनुरूप अनुकूलित (adapt) करना है।

questions.question_english: Under Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, which of the following pedagogical strategies are educational institutions statutorily mandated to adopt to ensure effective inclusion?
options_english: Establishing dedicated, segregated evening shifts exclusively for students with disabilities
Admitting students with disabilities strictly on the condition that parents arrange and pay for private special educators
Modifying the curriculum and examination systems to cater to the diverse learning needs of students
Restricting participation in physical education and sports activities to non-disabled students for safety reasons
questions.explanation_english:
Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 outlines specific measures required of educational institutions to achieve true inclusive education. Section 16(vi) mandates that institutions must:
'make suitable modifications in the curriculum and examination system to meet the needs of students with disabilities such as extra time for completion of examination paper, facility of scribe or amanuensis, exemption from second and third language courses.'

Options A, B, and D represent exclusionary, discriminatory, and unlawful practices. Section 16(i) mandates equal access to sports and recreation, Section 16(ii) requires accessible school infrastructure, and Section 16(iv) requires state-funded institutions to provide necessary individualized support without imposing financial burdens on parents.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 16 समावेशी शिक्षा को वास्तविक रूप देने हेतु शिक्षण संस्थानों के विशिष्ट कर्तव्यों को रेखांकित करती है। धारा 16(vi) के अनुसार संस्थानों को:
'दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए पाठ्यक्रम और परीक्षा प्रणाली में उपयुक्त संशोधन करना होगा, जैसे परीक्षा पूरी करने के लिए अतिरिक्त समय, श्रुतलेखक की सुविधा और द्वितीय व तृतीय भाषा के पाठ्यक्रमों से छूट।'

विकल्प A, B और D अलगाववादी, भेदभावपूर्ण और अवैध प्रथाएं हैं। धारा 16(i) स्पष्ट करती है कि दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों को खेलकूद और मनोरंजन गतिविधियों में दूसरों के समान समान अवसर दिए जाएंगे तथा धारा 16(iv) के तहत आवश्यक सहायता विद्यालय और शासन द्वारा उपलब्ध कराई जाएगी, न कि अभिभावकों पर निजी शिक्षक रखने की शर्त थोपी जाएगी।

एकीकृत शिक्षा (Integrated Education)

questions.question_english: What is the specific statutory term defined in Section 2(m) of the RPwD Act, 2016 for an educational system where students with and without disabilities learn together and the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted?
options_english: Special Education
Integrated Education
Mainstreaming
Inclusive Education
questions.explanation_english:
Section 2(m) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 defines 'inclusive education' as:
'a system of education wherein students with and without disability learn together and the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted to meet the learning needs of different types of students with disabilities.'

This marks a profound pedagogical shift from 'Special Education' (which isolates students with disabilities into segregated institutions) and 'Integrated Education' (which places disabled children in general schools without adapting the underlying curriculum or infrastructure). Inclusive education demands systematic restructuring of physical classrooms, pedagogical materials, teacher training, and assistive aids to foster universal accessibility and belonging.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 2(m) में 'समावेशी शिक्षा' (Inclusive Education) को स्पष्ट रूप से परिभाषित किया गया है:
'समावेशी शिक्षा से ऐसी शिक्षा प्रणाली अभिप्रेत है जिसमें दिव्यांगता वाले और दिव्यांगता रहित विद्यार्थी एक साथ सीखते हैं और शिक्षण एवं सीखने की प्रणाली को विभिन्न प्रकार के दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की अधिगम आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करने के लिए उपयुक्त रूप से अनुकूलित किया जाता है।'

यह संकल्पना 'विशेष शिक्षा' (जिसमें दिव्यांग बच्चों को अलग विशेष स्कूलों में रखा जाता है) और 'एकीकृत शिक्षा' (जिसमें बिना पाठ्यक्रम बदले बच्चे को केवल सामान्य स्कूल में बैठा दिया जाता है) से भिन्न और श्रेष्ठ है। समावेशी शिक्षा विद्यालयी वातावरण, पाठ्यक्रम, शिक्षण विधियों और मूल्यांकन में सर्वांगीण अनुकूलन की मांग करती है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 defines inclusive education as a system of education where students with and without disabilities learn together in the same classrooms. Under this framework, the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted to meet the diverse educational, social, and physical needs of all types of learners.

questions.question_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 के अंतर्गत शैक्षणिक संस्थानों और सरकारों के लिए निर्धारित निम्नलिखित कर्तव्यों एवं उपायों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. व्यक्तिगत आवश्यकताओं के अनुरूप समुचित वास-सुविधा (Reasonable accommodation) प्रदान करना।
II. दिव्यांग बच्चों को तथा उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों के सहायकों को परिवहन सुविधाएं उपलब्ध कराना।
III. विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता (Specific Learning Disabilities) की शीघ्र पहचान करना और उनके निवारण हेतु शैक्षणिक उपाय करना।
IV. सभी दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों को निःशुल्क विशिष्ट वर्दी (Specialized uniforms) उपलब्ध कराना।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-से कर्तव्य अधिनियम के अंतर्गत कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल I, III और IV
केवल II, III और IV
I, II, III और IV

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider the following duties and measures prescribed for educational institutions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016:
I. Providing reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements.
II. Providing transportation facilities to children with disabilities and to the attendants of children with high support needs.
III. Ensuring early detection of specific learning disabilities and taking pedagogical measures to address them.
IV. Supplying specialized uniforms free of cost to all students with disabilities.
Which of the duties given above are legally mandated under the Act?
options_english: I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I, II, and III are statutory mandates under Chapter III (Education) of the RPwD Act, 2016, whereas Statement IV is not:

- Statement I is correct: Section 16(iii) requires institutions to 'provide reasonable accommodation according to the individual's requirements'.
- Statement II is correct: Section 16(viii) mandates institutions to 'provide transportation facilities to the children with disabilities and also the attendant of the children with disabilities having high support needs'.
- Statement III is correct: Section 17(d) directs the appropriate government and local authorities to establish mechanisms to 'detect specific learning disabilities in children at the earliest and take suitable pedagogical and other measures to overcome them'.
- Statement IV is incorrect: While Section 16(vii) mandates the supply of books, learning materials, and appropriate assistive devices free of cost up to the age of 18 years, the statute does not mandate supplying 'specialized uniforms free of cost'.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I, II और III दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के अध्याय III (शिक्षा) के अंतर्गत कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य हैं, जबकि कथन IV अधिनियम में सम्मिलित नहीं है:

- कथन I सही है: धारा 16(iii) के अनुसार प्रत्येक बच्चे की व्यक्तिगत आवश्यकता के अनुसार समुचित वास-सुविधा (Reasonable accommodation) प्रदान करना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 16(viii) स्पष्ट रूप से आदेश देती है कि शिक्षण संस्थान 'दिव्यांग बच्चों को तथा उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों के सहायकों (attendants) को भी परिवहन सुविधाएं प्रदान करेंगे'।
- कथन III सही है: धारा 17(d) सरकार और स्थानीय प्राधिकरणों को यह दायित्व सौंपती है कि वे बच्चों में विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता (SLD) की शीघ्र पहचान करें तथा उपयुक्त शैक्षणिक उपाय अपनाएं।
- कथन IV गलत है: धारा 16(vii) के तहत 18 वर्ष की आयु तक निःशुल्क पुस्तकें, शिक्षण सामग्री और उपयुक्त सहायक उपकरण (Assistive devices) प्रदान करने का दायित्व है, परंतु 'निःशुल्क विशिष्ट वर्दी' प्रदान करने का कोई विधिक आदेश नहीं है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 mandates educational institutions to provide reasonable accommodation, ensure suitable transportation facilities for children with disabilities, and conduct periodic screenings for early detection of learning disabilities. Providing specialized uniforms free of cost is not a statutory duty prescribed under this specific section of the Act.

questions.question_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 के संस्थागत व प्रशासनिक ढांचे के संदर्भ में एक नामित 'मूल्यांकन बोर्ड' (Assessment Board / प्रमाणन चिकित्सा प्राधिकरण) की प्राथमिक भूमिका क्या है?
options_hindi: विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों (CWSN) के शैक्षणिक प्रदर्शन का सतत मूल्यांकन करना और ग्रेड प्रदान करना

विशेष आवासीय विद्यालयों के वित्तीय व्ययों का वैधानिक ऑडिट करना और सरकारी अनुदानों का निरीक्षण करना

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english: In the context of the institutional and regulatory framework of the RPwD Act, 2016, what is the primary role of a designated 'Assessment Board' / Certifying Medical Authority?
options_english: To continuously evaluate the academic progress and assign grades to children with special needs (CWSN)
To assess, quantify, and certify the nature and degree of disability for the issuance of a disability certificate
To conduct statutory financial audits and inspect state grants allotted to special residential schools
To recruit, train, and deploy certified special educators across state-run government schools
questions.explanation_english:
Under Sections 56, 57, and 58 of the RPwD Act, 2016, the appropriate government designates medical authorities / Assessment Boards comprising specialized medical practitioners and experts.

The primary function of an Assessment Board is to examine an applicant, verify and quantify the extent and nature of their impairment using standardized medical evaluation guidelines issued by the Central Government, and issue an official Certificate of Disability (and UDID - Unique Disability ID card). Furthermore, under Section 58(2), the Assessment Board evaluates whether an individual meets the threshold of a 'person with high support needs'. This certification is the sine qua non (essential legal document) for availing statutory reservations in education (Section 32), public employment (Section 34), and state welfare schemes.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 56, 57 एवं 58 के अंतर्गत समुचित सरकार द्वारा चिकित्सा विशेषज्ञों और डॉक्टरों से युक्त मूल्यांकन बोर्ड (Assessment Board / Certifying Authority) अधिसूचित किए जाते हैं।

इस बोर्ड का प्राथमिक कार्य केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिसूचित दिशानिर्देशों के आधार पर आवेदक की शारीरिक/मानसिक क्षति का चिकित्सकीय परीक्षण करना, दिव्यांगता की प्रकृति और उसके प्रतिशत का निर्धारण करना तथा आधिकारिक दिव्यांगता प्रमाण पत्र (Disability Certificate / UDID) जारी करना है। धारा 58(2) के तहत यह बोर्ड 'उच्च सहायता की आवश्यकता' का भी प्रमाणीकरण करता है। यह प्रमाण पत्र शिक्षा में आरक्षण (धारा 32), सरकारी नौकरियों में आरक्षण (धारा 34) तथा अन्य सामाजिक सुरक्षा योजनाओं का लाभ प्राप्त करने हेतु अनिवार्य विधिक दस्तावेज है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) To assess the nature and degree of disability for certification

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: for certification An Assessment Board constituted under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act of 2016 functions as a specialized medical evaluation body. Its primary responsibility is to assess, quantify, and certify the nature, extent, and percentage of disability in individuals, thereby issuing official disability certificates required to claim statutory reservations, welfare schemes, and supportive services.

questions.question_english: According to Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016, what is the minimum percentage of vacancies mandated to be reserved for persons with benchmark disabilities in every Government establishment?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 34(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 provides:
'Every appropriate Government shall appoint in every Government establishment, not less than four per cent. of the total number of vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts meant to be filled with persons with benchmark disabilities...'

This statutory provision represents a landmark increase from the 3% quota originally prescribed under Section 33 of the erstwhile Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995. Note the distinction: employment reservation under Section 34 is 4%, whereas reservation in higher education under Section 32 is 5%.

'प्रत्येक समुचित सरकार प्रत्येक सरकारी प्रतिष्ठान में बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले व्यक्तियों से भरे जाने वाले पदों के प्रत्येक समूह में संवर्ग क्षमता की कुल रिक्तियों में से कम से कम चार प्रतिशत (4%) पदों पर ऐसे व्यक्तियों को नियुक्त करेगी...'

यह पूर्ववर्ती दिव्यांगजन (समान अवसर, अधिकारों का संरक्षण और पूर्ण भागीदारी) अधिनियम, 1995 के तहत दिए गए 3% आरक्षण से 1% अधिक (अर्थात 4%) है। परीक्षार्थी ध्यान रखें कि सार्वजनिक रोजगार (Employment) में आरक्षण 4% है, जबकि उच्च शिक्षा में प्रवेश (Higher Education Admissions) हेतु धारा 32 के तहत यह 5% है।

questions.question_english: Within the mandated 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in public employment under Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016, what specific percentage is allocated to the category of 'deaf and hard of hearing'?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 34(1) of the RPwD Act, 2016, the overall 4% reservation in government vacancies is compartmentalized across five specific disability groups as follows:
(a) Blindness and low vision: 1%
(b) Deaf and hard of hearing: 1%
(c) Locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims, and muscular dystrophy: 1%
(d) Autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability, and mental illness: combined with (e) Multiple disabilities from amongst persons under clauses (a) to (d) including deafblindness: 1%

Together, categories (a), (b), (c) receive 1% each, and combined categories (d) and (e) receive 1%, making up the total 4% reservation. Thus, the category of deaf and hard of hearing is allotted exactly 1%.

(क) अंधता और कम दृष्टि (Blindness and low vision): 1%
(ख) बधिर और श्रवण बाधित (Deaf and hard of hearing): 1%

(घ) स्वलीनता (Autism), बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता, विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता और मानसिक बीमारी, तथा (ङ) खंड (क) से (घ) के अंतर्गत बहु-दिव्यांगता जिसमें बधिर-अंधता शामिल है: दोनों को मिलाकर 1%

questions.question_english: Can a Government establishment be exempted from the mandatory provision of reserving vacancies for persons with benchmark disabilities under the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: No, reservation in public employment is an absolute statutory right and no establishment can be exempted under any circumstances
Yes, the appropriate Government may, by notification and having regard to the type of work carried on, exempt any establishment
Yes, the Head of the Department has independent discretionary power to grant an exemption if eligible candidates are not available
Yes, but such statutory exemptions are legally permissible only for designated Group D operational posts
questions.explanation_english:
While Section 34(1) of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates a minimum 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in every Government establishment, the first proviso to Section 34(1) expressly provides for exemptions:
'Provided that the appropriate Government may, having regard to the type of work carried on in any department or establishment, by notification and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified in such notification, exempt any establishment from the provisions of this section.'

Such exemption cannot be granted arbitrarily or by an individual Head of Department; it requires an official gazette notification by the appropriate Government (Central or State Government), typically in consultation with the Chief Commissioner or State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (e.g., combatant units of armed forces or paramilitary forces).
questions.explanation_hindi:
यद्यपि RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34(1) प्रत्येक सरकारी प्रतिष्ठान में बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों के लिए 4% आरक्षण अनिवार्य करती है, परंतु धारा 34(1) का प्रथम परंतुक (proviso) विशिष्ट छूट का अधिकार देता है:
'परंतु समुचित सरकार किसी विभाग या प्रतिष्ठान में किए जाने वाले कार्य के प्रकार को ध्यान में रखते हुए, अधिसूचना द्वारा तथा ऐसी शर्तों के अधीन, किसी भी प्रतिष्ठान को इस धारा के प्रावधानों से छूट दे सकती है।'

यह विधिक छूट किसी विभागाध्यक्ष के व्यक्तिगत विवेक पर निर्भर नहीं होती, बल्कि केवल समुचित सरकार (केंद्र या राज्य सरकार) द्वारा विधिवत गजट अधिसूचना जारी करके ही दी जा सकती है (जैसे सशस्त्र बलों या अर्धसैनिक बलों के लड़ाकू संवर्गों के लिए)।

questions.question_hindi: किसी सरकारी शिक्षण संस्थान में लिपिकीय संवर्ग की भर्ती के दौरान, बेंचमार्क दिव्यांग व्यक्ति के लिए आरक्षित रिक्ति उपयुक्त उम्मीदवार उपलब्ध न होने के कारण रिक्त रह जाती है। दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34(2) के अनुसार तत्काल विधिक प्रक्रिया क्या होगी?
options_hindi: उस रिक्ति को उसी चक्र में तुरंत अनारक्षित (de-reserved) कर सामान्य वर्ग के उम्मीदवार से भर दिया जाना चाहिए
उस रिक्ति को अनिवार्य रूप से आगामी (अगले) भर्ती वर्ष के लिए बैकलॉग रिक्ति के रूप में अग्रेषित (carried forward) किया जाना चाहिए
उस रिक्ति को स्थायी रूप से अनुसूचित जाति (SC) अथवा अनुसूचित जनजाति (ST) के आरक्षित पद में परिवर्तित कर देना चाहिए
भर्ती प्रक्रिया को पूरी तरह रद्द कर दिया जाना चाहिए तथा उस पद को स्थायी रूप से समाप्त कर देना चाहिए

questions.question_english: During the recruitment of clerical staff in a government educational institution, a vacancy reserved for a person with benchmark disability remains unfilled due to the non-availability of a suitable candidate. What is the mandatory immediate procedural step under Section 34(2) of the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: The vacancy must be immediately de-reserved and filled by a general (unreserved) candidate in that cycle
The vacancy must be carried forward to the succeeding recruitment year as a backlog vacancy
The vacancy must be permanently converted into an SC or ST reserved vacancy
The recruitment process must be completely cancelled and the post permanently abolished
questions.explanation_english:
Section 34(2) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 explicitly establishes the procedure for unfilled reserved vacancies:
'Where in any recruitment year any vacancy cannot be filled up under sub-section (1) due to non-availability of a suitable person with benchmark disability or for any other sufficient reasons, such vacancy shall be carried forward in the succeeding recruitment year...'

The statute further provides that if in the succeeding recruitment year also a suitable candidate from that specific category is unavailable, the vacancy may first be filled by interchange among the five specified disability categories. Only when there is no person with disability available even after interchange can the post be filled by appointing a person other than a person with disability. Therefore, the immediate mandatory procedural step is to carry forward the vacancy to the next recruitment year; immediate de-reservation is strictly prohibited.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 34(2) में रिक्त पदों को भरने की सुस्पष्ट प्रक्रिया विहित की गई है:
'यदि किसी भर्ती वर्ष में उपधारा (1) के अधीन कोई रिक्ति उपयुक्त बेंचमार्क दिव्यांग व्यक्ति के उपलब्ध न होने के कारण अथवा किसी अन्य पर्याप्त कारण से नहीं भरी जा सकती है, तो ऐसी रिक्ति को आगामी भर्ती वर्ष में अग्रेषित (carried forward) किया जाएगा...'

कानून आगे यह प्रावधान करता है कि यदि आगामी भर्ती वर्ष में भी उस विशिष्ट दिव्यांगता श्रेणी का उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी नहीं मिलता है, तो इसे पहले दिव्यांगता की अन्य श्रेणियों के बीच परस्पर बदलकर (interchange) भरा जाएगा। यदि इंटरचेंज के बाद भी कोई दिव्यांग व्यक्ति उपलब्ध नहीं होता है, केवल तभी उस पद पर गैर-दिव्यांग व्यक्ति की नियुक्ति की जा सकती है। अतः तात्कालिक अनिवार्य कदम उस रिक्ति को अगले वर्ष के लिए अग्रेषित (carry forward) करना है; रिक्ति का तत्काल अनारक्षण (de-reservation) पूरी तरह प्रतिबंधित है।

questions.question_english: Under the rules framed for employment of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) in the Central Government and GNCTD, what is the maximum upper age relaxation provided to a General (Unreserved) category candidate with benchmark disability applying for direct recruitment to Group 'C' and Group 'D' posts?

questions.explanation_english: Under the consolidated guidelines issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) and the Directorate of Education (GNCTD) aligned with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, candidates with benchmark disabilities belonging to the General/Unreserved category are entitled to an upper age relaxation of 10 years for direct recruitment to Group 'C' and 'D' (as well as Group 'A' and 'B') civil posts. For candidates belonging to the OBC category with benchmark disabilities, the relaxation is 13 years (10 + 3 years), and for SC/ST candidates with benchmark disabilities, it is 15 years (10 + 5 years). This affirmative measure accounts for the educational and physical rehabilitation delays often faced by persons with disabilities, ensuring substantive equality in public employment under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 34(2) of the RPwD Act, 2016, where in any recruitment year any vacancy cannot be filled up due to the non-availability of a suitable person with benchmark disability, or for any other sufficient reasons, such vacancy is carried forward to the succeeding recruitment year. If in the succeeding recruitment year also a suitable person with benchmark disability is not available, the vacancy may first be filled by interchange among the five specified disability categories (clauses (a) to (e)). Only when there is no person with disability available for the post in that year even after interchange, may the employer fill up the vacancy by appointment of a person other than a person with disability. Thus, 'interchangeability' specifically refers to exchanging unfilled reserved vacancies among designated disability categories.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34(2) के अनुसार, यदि किसी भर्ती वर्ष में बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों हेतु आरक्षित कोई रिक्ति उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी के अभाव या अन्य पर्याप्त कारणों से नहीं भरी जा सकती, तो उस रिक्ति को अगले भर्ती वर्ष में अग्रेषित (carry forward) किया जाता है। यदि अगले भर्ती वर्ष में भी उस विशिष्ट दिव्यांगता श्रेणी का उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी नहीं मिलता है, तो सबसे पहले उस रिक्ति को धारा 34(1) की पाँच श्रेणियों [(a) से (e)] के बीच परस्पर विनिमय (interchange) द्वारा भरा जा सकता है। विनिमय के बाद भी यदि कोई दिव्यांग व्यक्ति उपलब्ध न हो, केवल तभी उस पद को गैर-दिव्यांग व्यक्ति की नियुक्ति द्वारा भरा जा सकता है। अतः 'परस्पर विनिमेयता' का तात्पर्य आरक्षित रिक्तियों को विभिन्न दिव्यांग श्रेणियों में परस्पर स्थानांतरित करने से है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 22 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, every government establishment is mandated to maintain records regarding persons with disabilities employed, facilities provided, and other particulars, which must be open to inspection. Sections 75(1)(h) and 80(c) empower the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the Union level) and the State Commissioners (at the State/UT level) to monitor the implementation of the Act, look into complaints, and inspect records maintained by establishments. Under the Act, Commissioners have the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including the power to requisition and inspect public records to enforce compliance with reservation rosters and workplace accessibility norms.

questions.explanation_english: Section 23 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 explicitly mandates that every government establishment shall appoint a Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) and inform the Chief Commissioner or the State Commissioner of such appointment. Under Section 23(2), any person aggrieved by non-compliance with the provisions of Section 20 (non-discrimination in employment and provision of reasonable accommodation) may submit a complaint to the Grievance Redressal Officer. The officer is legally obligated to investigate the grievance and take remedial action within two weeks. The GRO also maintains a register of complaints to ensure institutional accountability in government schools and departments.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Government establishments are required to compute the 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities against the total number of vacancies in the cadre strength.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court of India in the Rajeev Kumar Gupta case clarified that reservation for PwBD applies to all identified posts, irrespective of whether they are filled by direct recruitment or promotion.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both statements are legally accurate and true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). Under Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016 and the landmark Supreme Court ruling in Union of India v. National Federation of the Blind (2013), reservation for persons with disabilities must be calculated based on the total number of vacancies across the cadre strength, not merely against vacancies in identified posts. Separately, in Rajeev Kumar Gupta & Ors. v. Union of India (2016), later reinforced in Siddaraju v. State of Karnataka (2020), the Supreme Court held that PwBD reservation extends to promotional posts as well as direct recruitment, overturning earlier government restrictions. Because Assertion (A) pertains to the computation base (cadre strength) while Reason (R) establishes the mode of appointment (promotions), R does not serve as the causal explanation of A.
questions.explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों कथन विधिक रूप से सत्य हैं, परंतु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34 और सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के ऐतिहासिक निर्णय 'यूनियन ऑफ इंडिया बनाम नेशनल फेडरेशन ऑफ द ब्लाइंड' (2013) के तहत यह स्थापित किया गया कि दिव्यांगजनों हेतु 4% आरक्षण की गणना संवर्ग (कैडर) की कुल रिक्तियों के आधार पर की जाएगी, न कि केवल चिन्हित पदों की रिक्तियों पर। वहीं, 'राजीव कुमार गुप्ता बनाम भारत संघ' (2016) तथा 'सिद्धराजू' (2020) मामलों में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने यह व्यवस्था दी कि दिव्यांगजनों के लिए आरक्षण पदोन्नति में भी लागू होता है। चूंकि कारण (R) पदोन्नति में आरक्षण के सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन करता है, यह इस बात की व्याख्या नहीं करता कि गणना संवर्ग संख्या के आधार पर क्यों की जाती है। अतः विकल्प (B) सही है।

questions.explanation_english: Section 45(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 mandates that all existing public buildings shall be made accessible in accordance with the rules formulated by the Central Government within a period not exceeding five years from the date of notification of such rules. The rules were notified on 15 June 2017, establishing a primary statutory target period of five years (by June 2022) for government departments, educational institutions, and public authorities to conduct structural access audits and complete necessary retrofitting (e.g., ramps, accessible toilets, lifts, and signage). Although the proviso allows extensions on a case-to-case basis based on state preparedness, the core statutory limit is five years.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 45(1) के अनुसार, सभी मौजूदा सार्वजनिक भवनों (जिनमें सरकारी कार्यालय, स्कूल, कॉलेज और अस्पताल शामिल हैं) को केंद्र सरकार द्वारा नियमों के अधिसूचित होने की तिथि से अधिकतम 5 वर्ष की अवधि के भीतर सुगम और बाधा-मुक्त बनाया जाना अनिवार्य है। चूंकि दिव्यांगजन अधिकार नियम 15 जून 2017 को अधिसूचित किए गए थे, अतः सभी प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए प्राथमिक कानूनी समय-सीमा 5 वर्ष (जून 2022) निर्धारित की गई थी, जिसके भीतर संरचनात्मक ऑडिट और रेट्रोफिटिंग कार्य पूरे करने थे।

questions.explanation_english: The Government of India launched the 'Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan' (also known as the Accessible India Campaign) on 3rd December 2015, on the occasion of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities. Executed by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, this flagship initiative aims to create a universally accessible, barrier-free environment across three key verticals: (1) Built Environment Accessibility (retrofitting public buildings, schools, and hospitals with ramps, grab bars, and accessible toilets); (2) Transportation System Accessibility (enhancing accessibility in railways, civil aviation, and state road transport); and (3) Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Ecosystem (making government portals and media accessible to screen-reader users).

questions.question_english: Beyond the physical built environment, the RPwD Act, 2016 requires accessibility in information and communication technology (ICT). For school administration, what does this statutory mandate primarily imply?
options_english: Ensuring school websites and digital learning materials are fully accessible to CWSN
Providing mandatory separate high-speed internet connections exclusively for students with disabilities
Mandating that only specialized schools are required to invest in ICT accessibility infrastructure
